name: execute_kip_readonly
description: Executes read-only KIP 2.0 (Knowledge Interaction Protocol) commands against your Cognitive Nexus — your persistent memory. Accepts KQL (FIND) and META (DESCRIBE / LIST / SEARCH / VERIFY / VALIDATE / PREVIEW / HISTORY / CHANGES / SNAPSHOT / EXPORT CAPSULE). State-changing KML is rejected here regardless of how it is labelled. Ground before you read precisely: SEARCH finds candidates, then read them by exact id. A SEARCH miss is not evidence of absence, and a SEARCH score is not confidence.

command.description: A single complete read-only KIP 2.0 command (FIND / DESCRIBE / LIST / SEARCH / VERIFY / VALIDATE / PREVIEW / HISTORY / CHANGES / SNAPSHOT / EXPORT CAPSULE). Mutually exclusive with operations.

operations.description: Several read-only KIP commands in one round-trip. Each is evaluated independently and per-operation errors are returned inline.

op_id.description: A request-local name so this operation's result can be correlated in the response.

parameters.description: Parameters scoped to this operation. They override shared parameters with the same keys.

read.description: Bind every operation to one readable cognitive state coordinate, so a multi-step read sees a consistent world.

snapshot_token.description: An opaque token from an earlier response. Do not parse or modify it. It is a coordinate, not an authority: current permissions always apply.

parameters.description: Values bound into the command's :placeholders. Binding is structural, never string interpolation: a placeholder must occupy a complete KIP value position (name: :name, LIMIT :limit, SEARCH CONCEPT :term). Do not embed one inside a quoted string such as "Hello :name". Parameter names match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.

dry_run.description: Validate the command(s) without executing them.
